entries.title: Whole End Track And Raised Water Service Bay
entries.description: One static railway end-track water-service bay scene, one scene and zero new standalone models. Four complete unit-scale original instances retain every raw GLB mesh, node hierarchy, triangle, normal and PBR: two entire straight tracks join end-to-end, one whole low buffer stands just beyond the terminal rail ends, and one entire qualified high reservoir with counterweighted raised spout stands beyond the buffer. Its long lateral mouth projects back above the empty terminal-track zone while the reservoir feet and hanging weight remain outside the track envelope. A new finite low ballast-look ground body and one continuous L-shaped slightly raised side-approach/operating pad establish a separate approach along the right flank and a cross-strip in front of the tank trestle, rather than putting another bench beside a through platform. The empty end-track apparatus-overhead relation differs from the old trolley-on-track maintenance stop and the parallel ramped passenger platform. No train, tender, water, working controls or added equipment; every reused whole model remains unchanged, with only complete translations. The low buffer is presented beyond the existing end and is not fitted or certified to the rail. The low pedestrian-looking pad has an unchanged finite edge, not an accessibility ramp. All new geometry is scene-only, not independently counted models. Static artistic composition only; no vehicle gauge fit, human clearance, navigation, track connection, loading/refilling, flow, pressure, motion, counterbalance, ground bearing, civil engineering or railway safety claim. Rigging animation and interaction not made or verified.

entries.title: Fixed Horizontal Runner and Stone Millroom Cutaway
entries.description: One newly authored complete static regional millroom cutaway. A real open-ended dry race lies between two full supporting masonry walls beneath the room. A whole horizontal radial paddle runner sits on a low bearing foot and shares one continuous vertical shaft with the complete broad upper and lower millstones above. The lower stone has a genuine shaft passage and sits on two whole exposed transverse floor joists; the upper stone has a real central feed eye. A full open tapering hopper and narrow throat stand on independent complete rear posts, tie and side seats. The retained room has a true rear window, two short side returns, a rear floor patch and a thick pitched rear roof section; the front walls, floor boards and front roof are deliberately omitted to reveal the continuous lower-runner to upper-stone relationship. Finite section faces are closed, not unfinished surface holes. This is neither the old vertically oriented twin-rim waterwheel on an external A-frame nor a standalone hand quern relocated indoors, and no old wheel, building or stone mesh is imported. Three opaque PBR roles, metres Z up, whole horizontal envelope centred, one architectural cutaway zero scenes. Dry unoccupied regional-inspired artwork, not an exact historic reconstruction or operational plan. No water, grain, grinding process, shaft rotation, bearing fit, transmission, hydraulics, energy output, food hygiene, access, loading, structure or engineering safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made or verified.

entries.title: Fixed Terraced Mass and Three Approach Shrine
entries.description: One newly authored complete stepped-platform-shrine architectural exterior. A single continuous thick grounded masonry body retreats through three broad raised terraces. Three whole lower approach flights converge at one full front landing; from there one continuous upper stair climbs through the terrace fronts to a complete small upper shrine chamber. That chamber has an actual front doorway, thick side and back walls, an internal floor and a full roof, not a dark doorway decal. All tier bodies, landing and stair runs are one shared-vertex closed material boundary without interior overlapping cell faces. This is not a repeated collection of old plinths or an isolated bifurcated stair with changed step count: the three approaches converge and then enter one higher temple-like whole atop a terraced grounded mass. Unlike the old sunken stepwell, routes rise above the surrounding ground toward a separate upper chamber rather than descending within a retaining enclosure to a well. No old stair, architecture or model mesh imported. Three opaque PBR roles, metres Z up and whole horizontal envelope centred. One complete architectural module zero scenes. Fictional regional ancient-inspired static art only, not a named sacred site, historic reconstruction, religious activity or construction plan. No accessible route, stair standard, handrail safety, host fit, material strength, foundation, load, manufacture or engineering safety capability. Rigging animation interaction not made or verified.

entries.title: Whole Enclosed Dry Rink and Exterior Service Apron
entries.description: One complete static enclosed dry ice-rink-like service-boundary scene, one scene and zero new independent models. A new scene-only rounded rectangular pale pad and a continuous low open-front perimeter wall distinguish an interior empty skating-shaped area from an exterior service apron. The entire previously qualified fixed partly closed roll shutter stands in the front wall opening; the complete qualified front-tank and rear-conditioner ice-machine appearance parks separately to the right outside the boundary. Both original units retain every mesh, full buffer, normal, opaque PBR and internal hierarchy at unchanged unit scale, under translation only. The machine is not underneath the low fixed curtain and no traversable doorway or vehicle fit is claimed. Unlike the old open football goal/trolley floor and four-station utility bay, this is an enclosed interior pad with an exterior service edge, not a substitution of machines at those original positions. Only the common slab, raised pale pad and continuous perimeter boards are new scene architecture; none is counted as a new standalone model. No people, snow, liquids, ice physics, markings, venue regulation, vehicle operation, refrigeration, shutter motion, sightline or human access, loads, installation or safety capability. Rigging, animation and interaction not made.

entries.title: Fixed L Slot Sleeve and Twin Lug Tube Display
entries.description: One newly authored complete fixed two-part pipe-connector illustrative display. A single continuous thick female tube wall contains two actual opposed open-ended L-shaped through paths, each with an axial mouth followed by a finite circumferential return and closed stop. A separate complete coaxial male tube has a real full-length bore and two integral radial lugs sharing its wall boundary. The halves remain axially separated on two whole short lower saddles and one common finite display bed so the positive ears and negative slot paths can be read without pretending that motion has been solved. Both whole mouths remain open. This is not the old external eccentric-cam lever sleeve or the interleaved three-jaw coupling with a separate spider insert: the new relation uses actual rim-open turning tracks and integral tube ears, without external levers, a closure disk or an elastomer insert. All geometry independently authored, no old connector meshes imported. Three opaque solid PBR roles, metres Z up, whole horizontal envelope centred, one connector display model zero scenes. Fixed artistic bayonet-style appearance only, not a weapon or tool blade. No insertion path, twist motion, locking, standardized fit, sealing, fluid flow, pressure, torque, load, manufacture, installation or mechanical safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made or verified.

entries.title: Fixed Opposed Hollow Dee Chambers and Return Yoke Display
entries.description: One wholly newly authored static scientific-apparatus cutaway exhibit. A complete grounded plinth carries one continuous thick return-yoke form, its lower arm, full rear upright and retained shortened upper arm. A broad lower pole-disc and round chamber floor carry two independent hollow horizontal D-shaped bodies on four short fixed support posts. Each has a closed curved back, thick floor and one genuine open straight mouth facing the other across a continuous central slot. After the first actual image looked like two solid half-discs, this first real visual repair explicitly removes the entire left D roof, retaining its true thick floor, curved wall, finite rim and open straight mouth; the right D keeps its complete roof. The newly exposed interior is an intentional cutaway, not a transparent trick or a hollow claim based only on a hidden sample. A thick rear curved chamber-wall sector remains, while the front wall and entire lid are deliberately omitted. Only the rear segment of the upper pole-disc remains, its flat cut chord explicitly exposing the foreground bodies. A continuous blank rectangular winding-case appearance surrounds the rear yoke, and two closed side-stem appearances meet the D-shell backs. Unlike the U-yoke hand-generator there is no rotating axial drum, winding loops, crank or split-ring brushes; unlike the opposed annular-bowl exhibit there is no shared axis, toroidal cavity, curved vane field or small central guide ring. All visible geometry is new and authored together as one complete exhibit, not old magnetic and pump parts arranged into a scene. One model zero scenes, four opaque constant untextured PBR appearances, metre game coordinates/native Z up and complete horizontal bounds centred over the whole plinth sole. Cyclotron-inspired schematic artistic exterior only, not an accurate scientific instrument or an engineering design. No particle source or beam, electricity, radiofrequency, accelerating field, vacuum, resonance, magnetic field, radiation, calibration, experiment, image, precision, functional electrode/feedthrough, manufacture, operation or safety capability is made or verified. Omitted casing and upper pole regions are deliberate visible cutaway scope, not missing promised opaque walls. Rigging animation interaction not made.

entries.title: Whole Haul Truck on Bridge and Ticket Service Entry
entries.description: One static vehicle reception and weighbridge-inspired display, one scene and zero new independent models. The complete existing rigid haul truck remains in its original raised-body pose and unit scale, with all four original tyre soles on one broad continuous scene-only bridge deck. Four low supporting pads connect that deck to the common finite ground slab; real open underside gaps remain between the pads. Two whole sloped scene-only approaches sit at opposite ends, with honest 40mm static separations from the deck, not a promised drivable surface. A complete existing ticket booth stands independently at the side with its genuine service window facing the truck side. Its original TICKETS lettering and striped roof remain unchanged: it is reused as a ticket-service booth, not relabelled as a calibrated weighing console. Broad front and rear empty strips and a separate booth-side area define the entrance composition. Unlike the old grader yard, all vehicle wheels bear on a central raised continuous deck rather than on side ground banks spanning a recessed trench; unlike the old carnival entrance, there is no pennant arch or pedestrian branch sign, and a whole vehicle-support bridge is the central station. Both whole old models retain every original local buffer, normal, PBR dictionary and internal hierarchy; only exact unit rigid placement and scene-only support geometry are new. No vehicle part, booth sign or body pose is altered or extracted. No load cells, weight display, weighing accuracy, driving, tipping, traffic procedure, tyre grip, axle rating, road compatibility, accessible passage, operating clearance, structural or workplace safety are made or verified. The raised empty truck body is a fixed art pose, not an instruction for real vehicle weighing. Rigging animation interaction not made.
